beats.text: Five books that don't just inform you — they slowly make you wiser.
One. Meditations — Marcus Aurelius. A powerful man reminding himself how to stay good and sane.
Two. Tao Te Ching — Lao Tzu. Eighty short verses on strength through softness and stillness.
Three. The Essays — Montaigne. The wisdom of doubting yourself honestly and often.
Four. Letters from a Stoic — Seneca. A friend, across two thousand years, on how to actually live.
Five. The Analects — Confucius. Short, practical lines on character, duty, and how to treat people.
Wisdom can't be rushed — but it can be borrowed. Full explainers of each are on the channel.
